cover letter
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.
3+ years of experience in providing engineering support within educational or research environments.
Prior experience with instructional labs covering electronics, controls, robotics, RF systems, or related disciplines is highly desirable.

Under the general direction of the Senior Development Engineer, provide engineering and technical support across the instructional laboratories within the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences (EECS). Assist faculty, instructors, principal investigators, and senior engineering staff in the setup, integration, testing, operation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of instructional and research laboratory equipment supporting electronics, embedded systems, controls, robotics, RF technologies, autonomous systems, and laboratory instrumentation.

Support the installation, configuration, integration, testing, maintenance, and troubleshooting of instructional laboratory technologies and related systems, including electronic circuits, sensors, embedded platforms, robotic systems, RF equipment, laboratory instrumentation, networked devices, and associated instructional technologies.

Assist in implementing and evaluating new laboratory technologies, equipment upgrades, and instructional infrastructure improvements while ensuring compatibility, reliability, maintainability, and compliance with established safety practices.

Work collaboratively with senior engineering staff, faculty, students, and technical staff during the planning, implementation, and maintenance of instructional laboratory projects. Assist in the development, configuration, testing, and documentation of laboratory systems to support instructional goals and hands-on learning.

Support the development, modification, testing, and troubleshooting of firmware and software for microprocessors, embedded systems, and laboratory equipment using appropriate development tools and engineering practices. Assist with hardware-software integration for robotics, embedded platforms, RF systems, sensors, and autonomous systems to ensure reliable operation and compatibility across instructional environments.

Participate in interdisciplinary projects involving engineering, computer science, data science, and other research areas by providing technical support for laboratory equipment, instrumentation, and instructional technologies.
Assist with the integration and testing of hardware, software, networking, control, and other instructional technologies used in laboratory and classroom environments.

Work closely with the Senior Development Engineer to provide technical support, guidance, and training to faculty, students, graduate student instructors (GSIs), lab assistants, and student employees on the proper operation of laboratory and instructional equipment, safety protocols, and best practices for laboratory experimentation.

Assist in evaluating and improving instructional laboratory infrastructure, equipment, and operational processes to support evolving instructional and research needs. Help configure, maintain, and troubleshoot laboratory environments supporting electronics, embedded systems, robotics, RF, wireless communication, and related instructional technologies.
Support the development of laboratory documentation, operating procedures, and training materials to promote safe, reliable, and effective use of instructional facilities.

Maintain accurate documentation of laboratory equipment, engineering projects, system configurations, maintenance activities, and technical procedures to support ongoing operations, troubleshooting, and future system enhancements.

Monitor the performance and condition of instructional laboratory equipment and instructional systems, identify equipment deficiencies, and assist in implementing timely corrective actions to ensure safe, reliable, and continuous operation.
Maintain technical documentation for integrated hardware-software systems, including electronics, embedded systems, communication interfaces, control systems, and related technologies.
Assist with equipment inventories, lifecycle tracking, preventative maintenance records, and documentation updates to support efficient laboratory operations.

Proficiency in using development tools for microprocessors (e.g., ARM, AVR, PIC, Intel), CAD tools (e.g., AutoCAD, SolidWorks), and other technologies relevant to electrical engineering, computer science, and autonomous or RF systems.
Commitment to fostering a positive and supportive learning environment, promoting hands-on learning and experiential education.
Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to analyze complex technical issues, propose solutions, and implement effective resolutions.
Effective communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work closely with diverse stakeholders including faculty, students, and technical staff.
Ability to work in a collaborative manner; identify challenges and barriers and recommend resolutions.
